rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate all six compounds, reveal critical pairs, and minimize the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The elution window will guide subsequent gradient trimming and selectivity tests.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000 and remains the benchmark. Shorten the gradient one step to test whether full resolution can be retained with an earlier last peak.

The shorter gradient retains maximum CRF, but the critical pair is now close to the resolution threshold. Increase temperature by one step to test whether selectivity permits further acceleration while preserving full resolution.
Maximum CRF is already secured. Raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten retention while slightly reducing gradient steepness, testing whether the critical pair remains fully resolved.

Increasing the starting organic fraction shortened retention and improved the critical-pair resolution. Continue by one grid step to seek a faster method with maximum CRF, while monitoring compression of the early peaks.

Raise the starting organic fraction another step to reduce the last-peak time while retaining the slightly shallower gradient. Monitor the early pair for loss of retention and the middle pair for resolution below 1.5.

Test one further increase in starting organic fraction to shorten the fully resolved separation. Both the early pair and the middle critical pair still have resolution margin, but this step will probe the onset of excessive initial elution strength.

Increase temperature one step to test whether its previously favorable effect on the middle pair restores full resolution while shortening retention. Monitor the early pair, whose resolution decreased with temperature in earlier runs.

Maximum CRF is restored at a last-peak time of 3.40 min. Shorten the gradient one step to probe the speed–resolution boundary; comparison with injection 8 will isolate the slope response at this trimmed starting composition.

Injection 8 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested. Probe a much steeper gradient for a possible elution-order reversal that separates the middle pair again, lowering the starting organic fraction to protect early-peak retention.

Reduce the final organic fraction to make the six-minute gradient nearly as shallow as injection 8, aiming to recover middle-pair resolution with a slightly earlier last peak. The final composition remains well above the observed elution window.

Lowering the starting organic fraction previously improved the critical middle pair and should also protect early-pair resolution. Test whether that benefit supports a steeper six-minute gradient while recovering maximum CRF near the fastest fully resolved result.

Raise temperature one step from injection 12 to seek a shorter separation and improved middle-pair selectivity. The early pair is the main risk, so this run will establish whether temperature can provide further acceleration without losing maximum CRF.

Explore a cooler, stronger-starting gradient as an alternative selectivity regime, with injection 8 retained as the fastest fully resolved benchmark. Lower temperature should protect early retention, while the stronger start and steeper slope may separate the middle pair after an elution-order reversal.

Test whether a stronger starting composition and lower temperature open a useful alternative separation of the middle pair. This is exploratory; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed method with maximum CRF.

Return to the successful 50 C selectivity regime and trim the gradient endpoint to just above the observed elution window. This slightly shallower slope than injection 12 should increase critical-pair resolution while keeping all six peaks within a short gradient.

Preserve injection 8's successful starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope while ending the programmed gradient after four minutes. The endpoint remains above its estimated last-peak elution composition, so this should retain maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Lower the starting organic fraction relative to injection 13 to recover early-pair resolution at 55 C. The resulting steeper slope may shorten the separation, while this run tests whether the middle pair retains sufficient temperature-driven selectivity.

Return to 50 C and increase the endpoint one step from injection 16 to shorten retention. This probes the critical-pair resolution boundary between the successful moderate slopes and the overly steep gradients, with injection 17 retained as the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a faster alternative in the low-temperature regime where the middle-pair separation improved in injection 15. This exploratory method risks compressing the early peaks; injection 17 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved benchmark.

Test a substantially shallower gradient at injection 20's starting composition and temperature to see whether the remaining critical pair gains resolution. The lower endpoint should still elute all compounds promptly, while the slower slope may also protect the final pair.

Return to the fastest confirmed fully resolved regime and lower the endpoint one step to build resolution margin around its critical pair. This should preserve maximum CRF while testing a more robust alternative to injection 17, with only a modest retention-time increase.

Lower temperature one step from injection 22 to improve the early pair, now the limiting separation. Its shallower gradient provides middle-pair resolution margin, so this tests a better-balanced, fully resolved method while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step from injection 23 to shorten retention, using its resolution margin and the resulting shallower slope to protect the middle pair. Monitor early-peak compression; injection 17 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use a slope between injections 17 and 22 to target full resolution with slightly more margin than the fastest confirmed method and less retention than injection 22. Maximum CRF is already secured; this final run refines the speed–resolution tradeoff without repeating a method.
